_comment: Nikhil Deshpande's rubric (docs/qualification-rubric.md) and the scope rules from docs/services.md, as data. Edited by humans, read by src/lib/qualification.ts. No model reads this at request time.

timeline._comment: services.md: design is 3-4 weeks, execution 8-16. qualified.md: the site must be available for execution within 8-10 weeks of the consultation, and nothing can be ready in under 6 weeks from today.

commercial._comment: services.md caps commercial at ~3,000 sq ft. T18 in the September log was declined at 180 sq ft as below minimum scope; the front desk gave 500 as the floor.

decision_maker._comment: qualified.md: the caller should decide, or be authorised. Researching for others is insufficient ON ITS OWN - T14 in the log passed because the parents will attend the consultation. So this is a soft criterion: unclear never declines by itself.

budget._comment: qualified.md: never probe, never quote. Only act when a VOLUNTEERED number is clearly below what the described scope costs. These floors are deliberately conservative - they exist to catch the T10 case (1-1.5 lakh for a kitchen and a bedroom), not to pre-qualify. Rupees.

_decline_rule: qualified.md: two or more criteria fail -> decline. One fail -> decline only when it is a hard criterion. Unclear on a hard criterion -> ask one question. Unclear on a soft criterion -> treat as qualified and note it.
